newsitem.title: CANADA: KPMG survey sees pickup in Canadian growth.
newsitem.headline: KPMG survey sees pickup in Canadian growth.

text.p: Canadian economic growth will accelerate in 1997 but unemployment will remain "uncomfortably high," said a survey by accounting firm KPMG, released on Thursday.
Canada's economy was expected to grow by about 3.0 percent in 1997, outpacing U.S. growth of about 2.5 percent, the survey said.

"The economists participating in this survey predict that Canada's economy will continue to improve," said Randy Dutka, a KPMG partner, in a statement. "One of the biggest changes is that we're seeing increasing optimism that the federal government is getting its deficit under control."

KPMG said survey participants expected interest rates and inflation to remain low in Canada. Increases in the consumer price index were expected to remain at 2.0 to 3.0 percent a year for the foreseeable future.
The unemployment rate was expected to be about 9.3 percent for 1997, close to twice the rate in the United States.
